definitions.explanation: Using a product, service, or system on a trial basis, typically before committing to full adoption, purchase, or employment. Common in software free trials, product demo programs, and employment probation contexts.

examples.japanese: ソフトを{試用|しよう}する。
{新製品|しんせいひん}の{試用|しよう}レポートを{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a report on trying out the new product.

examples.japanese: {購入前|こうにゅうまえ}に30{日間|にちかん}の{試用|しよう}{期間|きかん}を{設|もう}けております。
examples.english: We provide a 30-day trial period before purchase.

notes:
Compound of {試|し} ('try; test') and {用|よう} ('use'). Note that the reading しよう is shared by several common homophones — {使用|しよう} ('use'), {仕様|しよう} ('specifications'), {私用|しよう} ('personal use') — so context and kanji matter.

USAGE:
- Used as a noun and with する to form a verb: {試用|しよう}する ('to try out').
- Frequent in product marketing (free trials), software contexts, and HR (probationary employment).
- Note: for HR use, {試用期間|しようきかん} ('probation period') is standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {試用|しよう}する: to try out; to use on a trial basis
- {試用|しよう}{期間|きかん}: trial period; probation period
- {試用版|しようばん}: trial version (of software)
- {無料|むりょう}{試用|しよう}: free trial
- {試用|しよう}レポート: trial/review report

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {使用|しよう}: use; usage — everyday 'using'; not necessarily trial-based.
- {試|ため}し: trial; test — native Japanese reading; more casual, e.g., お{試|ため}し ('a trial; giving it a go').
- {体験|たいけん}: experience; trial experience — emphasizes first-hand experience, as in {体験版|たいけんばん} ('demo version').
- テスト: test — a general katakana word, used for testing in many contexts.
